task:
Self-service coordinator handoff, first slice (herdr side) [t-ic5rrxn3]

Goal: a coordinator session can hand its tenure to a fresh session of the
same agent kind (Claude or pi) by itself, triggered manually from its own
pane. Read the item t-ic5rrxn3 in TODO.md, ONLY its last three notes
(from "Round 20261012-192328-6320" to the end); they are the design.
Existing code to build on: src/cli/coordinator.rs (`coordinator
start|end|status|handoff --to PANE`), src/app/api/coordinators.rs
(tenures with an epoch, `handle_coordinator_handoff`), `herdr agent start
--kind <kind> --pane <pane> --prompt <text>` (src/app/api/agents.rs and
its CLI). Verify each of these names in the code before using it; if the
code disagrees with this task, stop with WORKER-BLOCKED.

Build:
1. `herdr coordinator ready --note <path>` from the coordinator's pane:
   herdr checks the caller holds the tenure (current epoch) and that its
   agent is at a turn end (not working), copies the note into herdr's
   state directory and records its sha256. It marks the tenure
   `frozen`: mutations that already check the tenure refuse a frozen or
   superseded caller (at least `coordinator handoff`, `todo resume`,
   `worker start`, `worker answer`, `worker ack` where they have the
   caller's pane; list any you could not fence).
2. `herdr coordinator handoff --successor` from the coordinator's pane
   (after `ready`): herdr writes a handoff manifest (JSON, versioned) to
   its state directory: epoch, its own snapshot of the tenure (repository,
   runs in flight for that repository with their ids and last event ids,
   owned workers, pending question ids), snapshot path and sha256, the
   frozen note copy's path and sha256, the old pane id and the agent kind.
   It opens a new pane in the old pane's tab (no focus change) and starts
   the same agent kind there with ONE launch prompt from a per-kind table:
   claude `/todo --handoff <absolute manifest path>`, pi
   `/skill:todo --handoff <absolute manifest path>`; any other kind is
   refused before anything starts (fail closed). No second message.
3. `herdr coordinator ack --epoch E --snapshot <sha256>` from the
   successor's pane: herdr validates the pending handoff (epoch, hash,
   caller is the started successor pane), then in one step advances the
   epoch, moves the tenure, worker ownership and the tab's coordinator
   role to the successor, and ends the old agent session (stop its agent;
   leave the pane closed or idle as existing helpers allow, say which).
   A stale or wrong ack is refused and changes nothing.
4. Failure: if the successor exits or reports a limit before its ack,
   the handoff aborts, the old tenure unfreezes and keeps authority, and
   one event/notice says so. No timers anywhere (no grace period).
   `coordinator status` shows a pending handoff's state.
5. Tests next to the code: table tests of every transition (active ->
   frozen -> successor started -> acked; abort paths; stale ack; ready
   without tenure; unknown kind refused), using AppState/App test helpers,
   no real agent process. A fake successor that "speaks the ack" is
   enough.
6. Docs: a short section for these commands in
   docs/next/website/src/content/docs/ where coordinator commands are
   documented (find it); keep it generic, no personal paths.

Out of scope: the todo skill text (lives outside this repo; the
coordinator handles it), the automatic context-size trigger, codex/agy.

ATTEMPT 2. Start from attempt 1's commit: run `git cherry-pick --no-commit
2cd7b8ad3` (it is in this repository), then fix the review findings
below on top, and make exactly ONE commit with everything. Do not redo
work that attempt 1 did right: the ready/successor/ack path, ack
validation, abort on exit/limit/pane close, schema, tests.

Review findings to fix (file:line refer to commit 2cd7b8ad3):
1. The fence covers only some methods (src/api/workers.rs:180-300).
   Also fence for a frozen or superseded caller: WorkerPrompt,
   WorkerInterrupt, WorkerStop, WorkerKill, WorkerDenyAndStop,
   WorkerEscalate, TodoRunAnthropic, TodoStop, TodoCancelPending,
   TodoNext, TodoQueueSet, TodoGrant, TodoRevoke, and `coordinator end`
   from the frozen pane (today it silently drops the handoff,
   src/app/api/coordinators.rs:462). A test per newly fenced method
   family.
2. Nothing refuses a superseded caller: after ack the old pane passes
   every fence. Record the superseded pane and agent session ids on the
   tenure and refuse their mutations with a clear error. In
   `handle_coordinator_ack` the result of `close_pane` is discarded
   (`let _ = self.close_pane(...)`): if closing fails, the ack must not
   report success silently; the old session stays fenced as superseded
   either way, and the reply says the old pane could not be closed.
   `fence_worker` must fence by caller, not by owner: the user's own
   answers to escalated questions (not from the frozen pane) stay
   allowed while the tenure is frozen.
3. A successor that never produces an event (crash before detection,
   shell left in the pane, a trust or permission dialog) leaves the
   tenure frozen forever (coordinator_handoff.rs:473-503). Add `herdr
   coordinator handoff --abort` (from the old pane, the successor pane,
   or outside a pane with `--id`), and abort also when the successor is
   reported Blocked before its ack. No timers.
4. The pending handoff lives only in memory (registry.rs:82). Persist it
   with the registry's existing durable state (atomic write), restore it
   at startup and across a live handoff: re-register the successor pane
   so its exit is still reported, keep the old tenure frozen while the
   successor is pending, and add a test that a restored pending handoff
   accepts the ack and that a restored one whose successor pane is gone
   aborts with the one notice.
5. Fence-lift window in the ack (coordinator_handoff.rs:446-449 and
   coordinators.rs:711): validate, remove and transfer under one lock
   acquisition.
6. Refuse a relative `note_path` in the server (coordinator_handoff.rs:173),
   not only in the CLI.
Keep as is (decided by the coordinator): `ready` inside the turn
(document it), manifest and note copies kept after the handoff for audit.

worker_final_text:
The branch holds one commit, `cbe26c7b8`, with the subject you gave. The old pane is closed through `close_pane`, and if that fails the old session stays fenced as superseded. I could not run `just lint`, `just maintenance-test` or the full `cargo nextest run` successfully here, so those are not green; details below.

**Fixes for the review findings**
1. **Fences.**
   - These now refuse a frozen or superseded caller: `worker.prompt`, `interrupt`, `stop`, `kill`, `answer`, `ack`, `escalate`, `todo.run`, `run_anthropic`, `draft_run`, `cancel_pending`, `resume`, `next`, `stop`, `queue_set`, `grant`, `revoke` and `coordinator end`.
   - The fence works by caller pane, not by worker owner. A caller with no pane (the user's shell) is never fenced. One test, `a_frozen_or_superseded_caller_is_refused_by_every_mutation_family` in `src/api/workers.rs`, covers every family.
   - **`worker.answer` and `worker.deny_and_stop` cannot be fenced.** Their wire shapes are frozen by `advertised_client_shell_method_shapes_stay_at_the_v1_contract`, so they carry no caller pane. For `worker.answer` I added a new method, `worker.answer_from_pane`, which the CLI sends when it runs inside a pane. `worker.deny_and_stop` is a client click with no CLI command, so no coordinator sends it.
2. **Superseded sessions.**
   - The old pane and session ids are recorded after the ack and refused with `coordinator_superseded`.
   - The ack reply is a new `coordinator_acked` response with `old_pane_closed` and `close_error`. A failed close is reported, not hidden.
3. **Abort.**
   - New method `coordinator.handoff_abort` and CLI `herdr coordinator handoff --abort [--id]`, usable from the old pane, the successor pane, or outside a pane with `--id`.
   - A Blocked successor also aborts. No timers.
4. **Persistence.** Pending handoffs and superseded entries go to `<worker dir>/handoffs/pending.json`, written atomically, and are restored at startup. Restore re-registers the successor pane and keeps the old tenure frozen. Tests cover a restored handoff accepting the ack, one whose successor pane is gone aborting with one notice, and one whose tenure ended being dropped.
5. **Ack lock.** Validate, remove and transfer now happen under one registry lock.
6. **Relative `note_path`.** The server now refuses it with `invalid_request`.

I also regenerated `docs/next/api/herdr-api.schema.json`, and updated `socket-api.mdx` and `cli-reference.mdx`. They document `ready` inside the turn, `--abort`, the superseded behavior and persistence. I removed a stray empty `src/lib.rs` before committing.

**Checks**
- **Passed:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (the `just lint` command, run directly because `herdr-job slot` is blocked in the sandbox); `python3 scripts/windows_cross.py lint`; `just ui-hot-path-architecture-test`; the new handoff and fence tests; the schema-artifact test; and the v1 shape test. I did not run `cargo nextest run -E 'test(/workers::/)'` on its own. The earlier run over `handoff|coordinator|workers::` passed apart from sandbox socket failures, and the full-suite failures include 11 `workers::` socket tests.
- **Could not run cleanly (sandbox):**
  - **`cargo nextest run`:** I could not run it cleanly. `/var/folders/...` and Unix sockets are blocked, so I set `TMPDIR` to my own temp dir for the test runs. 520 tests still fail. In the final full run I filtered out the ones that panic with a permission, socket or PTY error and went through the remaining 53 names by hand. All are PTY or socket tests in unrelated areas (`app::api::*`, `persist::restore`, `server::*`, `api::server`).
  - **`just lint` and `just maintenance-test`:** `just lint` needs a slot file outside the working directory. 25 `maintenance-test` tests fail with `PermissionError`, in `test_awaiting_reply_audit` (the stall check) and `test_release`, none of which I touched.
- **Not needed:** `just integration-assets-test` and `just docs-contract-test`, since neither `src/integration/assets/` nor `scripts/docs/` is touched.
- **Not run:** no live end-to-end handoff against a running server.

WORKER-DONE cbe26c7b8 | review fixes: caller-based fences (worker.answer_from_pane added; worker.answer and worker.deny_and_stop left unfenced to keep their v1 shapes), superseded fence, coordinator.handoff_abort and --abort, persisted pending handoffs, single-lock ack, relative note path refused; sandbox blocks the full nextest run, just lint and maintenance-test

expected.summary: A successor reported Blocked aborts the handoff, although a permission or trust prompt is a normal part of its startup.
At server start an owner pane whose agent is not detected yet is reported as exited, which aborts a restored handoff whose successor is still starting.
The superseded fence matches only the pane id, so the old agent session resumed in another pane is not fenced.
The superseded fence matches only the pane id, so a new session reusing the old pane id after a restart is wrongly fenced.
The ack transfers the tenure even when persisting the new state fails, so the file and memory disagree about who holds it.
A failed state write on abort is only logged as a warning instead of being reported as an error.
